pending_commit.commit_message: CHROMIUM: drm/mediatek: crtc: Synchronously disable all overlays during crtc->enable During an atomic update, Mediatek DRM disables/enables crtcs and encoders first, and then applies plane state (enable/FB address) changes. On boot, firmware may have enabled some overlays, with an FB that is no longer mapped. Furthermore, drm/mediatek uses active_only, so state changes are only applied to hardware when the corresponding crtc is enabled. In other words, when disabling a CRTC, the CRTC's planes SW state is disabled, but the hardware state is not actually changed at disable time. Thus, like at boot, the overlay hw state will be 'enabled', but the scanout address points to an FB that has already been unmapped. To avoid an iommu fault between when we enable the encoder and when the new plane state is later applied to hardware in both of these cases, explicitly start all overlays in disabled state. The correct plane state for any enabled planes will be applied later in the atomic update. Also, since there is no active scanout anyway, do not wait for a vblank before starting the pipe; rather, just request an immediately synchronous cmdq update. Lastly, since we start the pipes with overlays disabled, we don't need to synchronously turn them off when disabling the crtc. CHROMIUM: drm/mediatek: Add a wait for vblanks during atomic_commit Originally, drm/mediatek did not wait for vblanks in atomic_commit to avoid blocking page flips on legacy cursor ioctl updates. However, this was not necessary, thanks to upstream commit a987cb3c04cf ("drm/atomic-helpers: Recover full cursor plane behaviour"), which uses a special legacy_cursor_update flag to skip actually waiting for vblanks when handling legacy cursor updates. Here is the atomic update flow: drm_atomic_helper_swap_state(drm, state); drm_atomic_helper_commit_modeset_disables(drm, state); drm_atomic_helper_commit_modeset_enables(drm, state); drm_atomic_helper_commit_planes(drm, state, true); drm_atomic_helper_wait_for_vblanks(drm, state); drm_atomic_state_free(state); The wait_for_vblanks means we can really free the atomic state (and thereby unreference the old FB) in state_free, since we are sure it is no longer onscreen [1]. Furthermore, it is required that the driver only permit one page flip per crtc vblank. [1] - well, at least we can for page flips. For the asynchronous legacy cursor ioctl we still need to hold a reference to the old FB past drm_atomic_state_free(), and free it later in a dedicated unreference worker that is triggered by vblank. CHROMIUM: soc: mediatek: CMDQ: cascade tasks to wait one vsync for display Our previous method is to merge all GCE commands into one task to wait one vsync event in display's target line interrupt. However, this method will shift 20% commands to next frame. Our new method is to flush all received commands from display to CMDQ, and then to consume all the flushed commands in vblank by CMDQ driver. However, every task contains one WFE command to wait vsync event. GCE will only execute one task for each vsync event. This patch provides a solution for this issue. It will keep WFE of first active task (in one of the GCE thread), and then remove WFE from other following active tasks. In other words, we cascade all flushed display tasks together to just wait one vsync event. Therefore, GCE can consume all active tasks in one vsync. This is a supporting patch for "CHROMIUM: drm/mediatek: remove target line interrupt" patch. CHROMIUM: soc: mediatek: CMDQ: fix WFE issue In merging WFE case, checking boundary condition is not enough for display. We should check if PC > WFE, i.e. GCE receive vsync event and start to execute. This is because inserting new task will suspend GCE and then GCE may access display registers outside vblank after resume. The solution is to wait for a while to let GCE finish its work if GCE has received vsync event. After that, we are safe to insert new task with WFE and the following tasks without WFE, i.e. new tasks should be executed by next vsync. BTW, we can remove boundary condition checking in merging WFE case. CHROMIUM: drm/mediatek: crtc: Remove cmdq_work and rework unreference work Previously, the command queue could only send one cmdq_rec per vblank. This limited the drm driver to only issue one atomic update per vblank. This is correct behavior for page flips, but it meant that the driver could not perform a legacy cursor ioctl and page flip in the same vblank, since that would require to atomic updates. Instead, the display driver collected commands from plane updates (primary and cursor) into "cmdq_pending" variables. The driver would then issue a single cmdq_rec with a wait of vblank to apply all pending changes to both primary and cursor planes. To ensure that this cmdq_rec was issued before vblank, the RDMA line interrupt was used to trigger an irq at 80% of frame duration. This irq would then schedule the cmdq work to actually create and submit the cmdq_rec to the command queue. The major disadvantage of this scheme, is that using the line irq throws away 20% of each frame. That is, if a page flip is requested after the line irq but before vblank, it would not get applied at the next vblank, instead it would be queued up and must wait as long as 120% of a frame period before it appearing on screen. Likewise, this would actually reduce frame rate, as userspace would also have to wait before it could submit the next page flip. To fix this, the command queue was updated to chain together atomic commits and apply them en masse at vblank. Therefore, the drm driver need no longer need to use the RDMA line irq to carefully time and apply cmdq_rec at 80% of frame duration. This patch removes the cmdq worker, and instead directly submits the cmdq_rec in atomic_flush. Furthermore, it starts the cmdq_rec in atomic_begin, and adds mtk_drm_crtc_plane_update to allow planes to request the crtc reprogram the display pipe components during atomic_update/disable(). Also, rather than tracking pending state in the struct mtk_drm_crtc, just use the struct drm_atomic_state, which already contains all of the information we need to know. In particular, during an atomic commit, the old drm_atomic_state holds a references to the old framebuffer that is coming ofscreen, that we will want to unreference once the flip is complete. For page flips an atomic commit is truly blocking - mtk_atomic_complete explicitly waits for the next vblank to confirm that a pending operation has completed before returning, and only one page flip is allowed per crtc per vblank. However, things get more complicated when dealing with the asynchronous legacy cursor. In order to possibly multiple cursor updates and page flips in a single vblank, there is a special "legacy_cursor_update" check that will skip waiting for vblank during an atomic cursor update. In other words, mtk_atomic_complete() finishes before it is confirmed that the update has really happened. If the cursor update is a cursor *disable* this means mtk_atomic_complete will finish while the old cursor FB is still being scanned out. However, once mtk_atomic_complete() finishes, the DRM core & userspace are free to drop all of their references on the cursor FB, which could lead to iommu faults. To avoid this, the current mtk_crtc layer takes an extra reference on each FB, and then uses a complicated scheme to manually track the state of FBs (new/onscreen/fb) to ensure that last reference is only dropped once the FB is truly no longer onscreen. The scheme uses a work, because the signal indicating that the FB is offscreen is handled in an interrupt handler, and unreferencing framebuffers is forbidden in atomic (or isr) context. This patch uses the information already stored in the drm_atomic_state itself to keep track of the "old FB" that should be freed. To ensure this information is available in the special case where we want to unreference and FB but mtk_atomic_complete() doesn't wait for vblank, we use a kref to pin the atomic state until it is released by both mtk_atomic_complete(), and by the unreference worker. The unreference worker is moved from the crtc layer up to the mtk_drv layer, since it is now unreferencing the whole drm_atomic_state, not just the old FB. Cleaning up the old RDMA line interrupt is left for a follow-up patch. CHROMIUM: drm/mediatek: Remove 'flip complete' completion The cmdq will now concatenate multiple cmdq_recs. In particular, during mtk_crtc_ddp_hw_fini(), the 'stop' command will now be appended to all pending page flip/cursor movements. Thus, the cmdq_rec_flush() after 'stop' becomes a synchronization point, which guarantees that any and all pending cmdq transactions have completed. Therefore, the 'completion' object, which was attempting to do the same thing, is now redundant. Furthermore, the completion didn't actually work, since it could only guarantee that a single pending transaction was complete; it does not actually properly handle concatenation. As a side-effect, we must also move the drm_crtc_vblank_off() after 'stop', to ensure that we still process any final pending vblanks prepended to 'stop'. Lastly, move drm_crtc_vblank_on() inside mtk_crtc_ddp_hw_init() for symmetry. UPSTREAM: lenovo/x200,t400: enable C4 cpu low power state This enables the C4 low power state on the lenovo x200 and t400. It's inspired by the thread on the mailinglist: "[coreboot] Lenovo X200 running Coreboot drains 3-4W more power than with Vendor BIOS". What this does, is to enable a C3 state using MWAIT(C3) request and set the southbridge config c4onc3_enable to automatically upgrade C3 to the lower power C4 state. The latency (0x37) is the same value used by the vendor bios. With C4 enabled the idle power consumption is about ~2-3W lower. TEST= build and install on target. UPSTREAM: cbfs: Add "struct" file type and associated helpers This patch adds functionality to compile a C data structure into a raw binary file, add it to CBFS and allow coreboot to load it at runtime. This is useful in all cases where we need to be able to have several larger data sets available in an image, but will only require a small subset of them at boot (a classic example would be DRAM parameters) or only require it in certain boot modes. This allows us to load less data from flash and increase boot speed compared to solutions that compile all data sets into a stage. Each structure has to be defined in a separate .c file which contains no functions and only a single global variable. The data type must be serialization safe (composed of only fixed-width types, paying attention to padding). It must be added to CBFS in a Makefile with the 'struct' file processor. UPSTREAM: cbmem: Always maintain backing store struct in a global on non-x86 The current CBMEM code contains an optimization that maintains the structure with information about the CBMEM backing store in a global variable, so that we don't have to recover it from cbmem_top() again every single time we access CBMEM. However, due to the problems with using globals in x86 romstage, this optimization has only been enabled in ramstage. However, all non-x86 platforms are SRAM-based (at least for now) and can use globals perfectly fine in earlier stages. Therefore, this patch extends the optimization on those platforms to all stages. This also allows us to remove the requirement that cbmem_top() needs to return NULL before its backing store has been initialized from those boards, since the CBMEM code can now keep track of whether it has been initialized by itself. FROMLIST: ath10k: fix throughput regression in multi client mode commit 7a0adc83f34d ("ath10k: improve tx scheduling") is causing severe throughput drop in multi client mode. This issue is originally reported in veriwave setup with 50 clients with TCP downlink traffic. While increasing number of clients, the average throughput drops gradually. With 50 clients, the combined peak throughput is decreased to 98 Mbps whereas reverting given commit restored it to 550 Mbps. Processing txqs for every tx completion is causing overhead. Ideally for management frame tx completion, pending txqs processing can be avoided. The change partly reverts the commit "ath10k: improve tx scheduling". login: Make RemoveArcData() more reliable Previously, the function simply removed android-data/, but it turns out that the implementation doesn't always work. There is currently no easy way for signer scripts to figure out if the image should use dev_firmware or not except looking into keyset folder. FROMLIST: ath10k: improve wake_tx_queue ops performance txqs_lock is interfering with wake_tx_queue submitting more frames. so queues don't get filled in and don't keep firmware/hardware busy enough. This change helps to reduce the txqs_lock contention and wake_tx_queue() blockage to being possible in txrx_unref(). To reduce turn around time of wake_tx_queue ops and to maintain fairness among all txqs, the callback is updated to push first txq alone from pending list for every wake_tx_queue call. Remaining txqs will be processed later upon tx completion. Below improvements are observed in push-only mode and validated on IPQ4019 platform. With this change, in AP mode ~10Mbps increase is observed in downlink (AP -> STA) traffic and approx. 5-10% of CPU usage is reduced. Major improvement is observed in 1-hop Mesh mode topology in 11ACVHT80. Compared to Infra mode, CPU overhead is higher in Mesh mode due to path lookup and no fast-xmit support. So reducing spin lock contention is helping in Mesh. FROMLIST: mmc: sdhci-of-arasan: Properly set corecfg_clockmultiplier on rk3399 corecfg_clockmultiplier indicates clock multiplier value of programmable clock generator which should be the same value of SDHCI_CAPABILITIES_1. The default value of the register, corecfg_clockmultiplier, is 0x10. But actually it is a mistake by designer as our intention was to set it to be zero which means we don't support programmable clock generator. So we have to make it to be zero on bootloader which seems work fine until now. But now we find an issue that when deploying genpd support for it, the remove callback will trigger the genpd to poweroff the power domain for sdhci-of-arasan which manage the controller, phy and corecfg_* stuff. So when we do bind/unbind the driver, we have already reinit the controller and phy, but without doing that for corecfg_*. Regarding to only the corecfg_clockmultipler is wrong, let's fix it by explicitly marking it to be zero when probing. With this change, we could do bind/unbind successfully.
